Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — our renewal with Redwood is coming up in April and the procurement team flagged a couple of items related to SOC2 evidence and log retention that I wanted to surface early. Specifically: 

- Aurora’s security team is requesting evidence retention for audit logs to cover 7 years for regulatory reasons (we currently keep 3).
- Our auditors (cc’d separately) want confirmation on where you will host exported logs and a short timeline for when evidence packages will be available during renewal.

We’re also evaluating a modest seat/throughput increase for the Dedicated capacity to support a new pilot — I expect procurement will request specific numbers later this week. Can we get a quick plan from you next steps and any constraints around retention policy changes and evidence exports?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: SOC2 evidence & retention question ahead of renewal

Hi Marissa — great to hear from you and thanks for the heads up.

High level responses:
- Retention: Redwood’s default audit log retention for hosted customers is 3 years. We can support extended retention up to 7 years, but longer retention impacts storage planning and will require a capacity uplift commitment (reserved capacity add-on or expanded Dedicated seats).
- Evidence package: we can produce a scoped SOC2 evidence bundle (controls matrix + supporting artifacts + log extracts) during the renewal window. For Aurora I recommend we produce an initial upload within the first 7 business days of the renewal period and a final, audited bundle within 21 days.

Next steps I propose: Jordan will put together a quick cost/throughput estimate for the seat uplift; Tessa will scope the evidence export process (locations, formats, retention buckets). Can we aim for a short sync (30 min) Thursday to align on procurement ask and timelines?

Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

- Timeline for evidence bundle: initial evidence upload to shared Drive within 5 business days post-renewal; full indexed package within 14 business days.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC2 evidence & retention question ahead of renewal

Ben / Marissa — thanks, all actionable items below and a brief mutual action plan.

1) Chain of custody (summary):
- Extraction: server-side export job from our audit pipeline to a signed S3 export (exports are generated as gzipped CSV with SHA256 checksum).
- Integrity: each export is hashed; checksums are published to the evidence index and verified by the receiving party.
- Encryption: data encrypted in transit (TLS1.3) and at rest (AES-256).
- Access controls: exported bundles stored in a dedicated evidence bucket with role-based access; only authorized Redwood security engineers and Aurora-designated readers are granted read role.

2) DocuSign & amendment: Jordan attached a redline earlier — I’ll ask Contracts to convert the attached PDF into a DocuSign-ready envelope and populate the pricing table (expected by EOD Wednesday). DocuSign link will be sent to Ben when ready.

3) Drive access: Tessa will create the evidence folder and grant Neil Baxter read-only access for the audit (temporary, will expire after 90 days) and will post the initial evidence index there.

4) Retention operational detail: 7-year retention will be implemented as follows: active 12 months in hot store, 6 years in cold store (retrieval SLA 48 hours). Additional monthly fee aligns with Jordan’s estimate; exact figures to be in the amendment.

Mutual action plan / dates:
- Wed 2027-03-10: Contracts issues DocuSign-ready amendment (Jordan/Vanessa)
- Mon 2027-03-15: Initial evidence upload to Drive (Tessa)
- Fri 2027-03-26: Final indexed evidence bundle uploaded (Tessa)
- Apr 01 2027: New term effective date (if amendment signed)

Let me know if you want to move any of the dates tighter — we can compress the evidence window if Aurora needs faster delivery, but that may shift the retrieval SLA and cost profile.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
